children: New Zealand's 3Q inflation data looked better than expected, but there's a sting in its tail. The signal on underlying inflation was more hawkish, says Sharon Zollner, chief economist at ANZ. Key trimmed mean measures, the weighted median, inflation ex-fuel and energy, and services inflation all accelerated in the quarter, which is an "unwelcome development," she said. Zollner characterises the data as "net hawkish." When combined with the weaker New Zealand dollar and higher oil prices, the data is likely to keep the Reserve Bank of New Zealand quite concerned about upside inflation risks for a while yet, she adds. (james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)
